instructions.primary_message: This recipe requires the dough to rise and rest for about 3 hours total in addition to mixing and baking time. Please plan accordingly!
Place warm water (105°F - 115°F), sugar, and yeast in a small bowl. Whisk to combine, then set aside until the yeast hydrates and becomes frothy, about 10 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 tsp granulated sugar
1 tsp instant dry yeast

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, place flour, additional sugar, baking powder, and spices in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a dough hook attachment. Whisk to combine, form a divot in the center of the flour mixture, and set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
4 cups bread flour
granulated sugar
1 tsp baking powder
½ tsp salt
⅛ tsp cardamom, ground
⅛ tsp nutmeg, ground

instructions.primary_message: Cut butter into small pieces. Place in a small saucepan, along with milk, then set over low heat; cook, stirring occasionally, until butter is melted, 3-4 minutes. Remove from heat and set aside to cool until the mixture is 110°F when measured with a thermometer, about 10 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
⅓ cup butter, unsalted
1 cup whole milk

instructions.primary_message: When the yeast is hydrated and the milk is cooled, add both to the bowl with the dry ingredients. Mix on low speed until dough is smooth and comes together on the hook attachment, 4-5 minutes.
Remove bowl from the stand mixer and cover with a dish towel or plastic wrap. Set aside in a warm area until the dough doubles in size, 2-3 hours.
Once the dough has doubled in size, coat two large baking sheet pans with ghee and set aside.
Turn the dough out onto a cutting board, then gently press to remove excess air. Cut the dough into 30 small pieces, about the size of a ping-pong ball.
Working one at a time, roll the dough balls into 2 ½-inch long logs. Overlap the two ends of the dough to form a ring, then arrange on the baking sheets, spacing rings about 1-inch apart.
Cover the baking sheets with dish towels or plastic wrap. Set aside to rest, until the dough rises slightly and holds an indent when lightly pressed with a finger, about 1 hour.
When the dough is almost ready, preheat the oven to 425°F.
Place baking sheets in the preheated oven and bake, rotating halfway through, until the ka'ak are golden, 12-15 minutes. Remove from the oven.
Meanwhile, melt ghee in a clean small saucepan. Remove from heat.
When the ka'ak are done, brush with melted ghee. Arrange on a platter and enjoy!
